questions.q: Why do neighboring propellers of a quadcopter spin in opposite directions?
options: The firmware requires it for the mixer
questions.explain: Each motor tries to turn the frame opposite to the prop's rotation. Two pairs spinning in opposite directions cancel this torque.

questions.q: How does a quadcopter turn in yaw?
options: It tilts all motors with servos
questions.explain: The difference in the reaction torques of the diagonal pairs creates a moment about the vertical axis while total thrust stays almost unchanged.

questions.q: What is a thrust-to-weight ratio (T/W) of 2:1?
options: Hover throttle of 20 % on a full battery
questions.explain: T/W = maximum thrust of all motors / takeoff weight. At 2:1 hover is at about half throttle — there is almost no margin for maneuvering.

questions.q: The drone flips over right on takeoff. The most likely cause?
options: High P and too powerful a battery
questions.explain: If the real build doesn't match the frame diagram in the firmware, the mixer commands the wrong motors, and the drone tumbles in a fraction of a second.

questions.q: Which control axis of a multirotor is the weakest, and why?
options: Pitch: the center of gravity is offset
Yaw: the reaction torque is small
questions.explain: Yaw is produced by reaction torque, which is much smaller than the moment from a thrust difference. So yaw is slower and is the first to hit motor saturation.
